{{Elections in Oregon}}
The '''2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Oregon''' will be held on November 8, 2022, to elect the six [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. representatives]] from the [[U.S. state|state]] of [[Oregon]], one from each of the state's six [[Oregon's congressional districts|congressional districts]]. Primaries for these seats were held on May 17, 2022. The elections will coincide with the elections and primaries of other federal and state offices.

District boundaries were redrawn<ref>{{cite web|last1=Hammond |first1=Betsy |last2=Friesen |first2=Mark |date=2021-10-03|title=Map: Look up how partisan your new legislative, congressional districts are in Oregon|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/data/2021/10/map-look-up-how-partisan-your-new-legislative-congressional-districts-are-in-oregon.html|access-date=2021-10-09|website=[[The Oregonian]] |language=en}}</ref> to ensure that the districts are [[United States congressional apportionment|apportioned]] based on data from the [[2020 United States census]], which added a sixth seat to Oregon's delegation.<ref name=opb/>

{{see also|Oregon's 1st congressional district}}
From 2012 to 2020, the 1st district was located in northwestern Oregon and included the western [[Portland metropolitan area|Portland metro area]], including the [[Portland, Oregon|Portland]] suburbs of [[Beaverton, Oregon|Beaverton]] and [[Hillsboro, Oregon|Hillsboro]], and parts of Portland west of the [[Willamette River]]. The district was kept largely the same despite redistricting, exchanging [[Yamhill County, Oregon|Yamhill County]] for [[Tillamook County, Oregon|Tillamook County]] and taking in more of Portland. The incumbent is Democrat [[Suzanne Bonamici]], who was re-elected with 64.6% of the vote in 2020.<ref name="HPVT"/>

{{see also|Oregon's 2nd congressional district}}
From 2012 to 2020, the 2nd district was the largest of Oregon's districts and covered roughly two-thirds of the state east of the [[Cascade Range|Cascades]], encompassing the [[Central Oregon|central]], [[East Oregon|eastern]], and [[Southern Oregon|southern]] regions of the state, including [[Bend, Oregon|Bend]] and [[Medford, Oregon|Medford]]. The district was kept mostly the same during redistricting, but it did lose Bend to the 5th district and [[Hood River County, Oregon|Hood River County]] to the 3rd, while taking in all of [[Josephine County, Oregon|Josephine County]] and about half of [[Douglas County, Oregon|Douglas County]]. The incumbent is Republican [[Cliff Bentz]], who was elected with 59.9% of the vote in 2020.<ref name="HPVT"/>

From 2012 to 2020, the 4th district included the southern [[Willamette Valley]] and the [[Southern Oregon Coast|South Coast]], including [[Eugene, Oregon|Eugene]], [[Corvallis, Oregon|Corvallis]], and [[Roseburg, Oregon|Roseburg]]. The new 5th district keeps the southern suburbs of Portland and reaches further into the city, but does not include any coastline, instead stretching southwards through the eastern parts of [[Marion County, Oregon|Marion]] and [[Linn County, Oregon|Linn]] counties to [[Bend, Oregon|Bend]]. 

The incumbent, Democrat [[Kurt Schrader]], was re-elected with 51.9% of the vote in 2020.<ref name="HPVT">{{cite web|last1=Wasserman|first1=David|last2=Andrews|first2=Sophie|last3=Saenger|first3=Leo|last4=Cohen|first4=Lev|last5=Flinn|first5=Ally|last6=Tatarsky|first6=Griff|title=2020 House Popular Vote Tracker|url=https://cookpolitical.com/2020-house-vote-tracker|publisher=Cook Political Report|access-date=May 10, 2021}}</ref> He lost renomination to [[Jamie McLeod-Skinner]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Centrist Schrader ousted in Oregon primary |url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/politics/centrist-schrader-ousted-in-oregon-primary/ar-AAXO5a9 |access-date=2022-05-27 |website=MSN |language=en-US}}</ref>
